findings.reason: without a stated order (run the A/B against the still-live comment path, then retire), a worker can delete the comment path first and lose the control arm the measurement depends on.
findings.text: §5 states "The free-text comment field remains for people and no code path reads it", yet its own done-when (line 190) requires "one refine rotation driven by checks with one driven by comments"; the comment-driven arm reads the comment field, and the section also retires the comment-driven refine instruction list in the same breath, so the node is asked both to keep the comment path alive for the A/B control and to make it unread.

findings.reason: the claim is imprecise as written, but no node's gate rests on the literal no-reader assertion (the done-when binds only `should_trigger_fanout`), so correcting the sentence does not change a measure or a delivered path.
findings.text: §5 asserts "no code path reads it" of the free-text comment field, but `imas_codex/standard_names/chain_history.py:43` (name axis) and `:88` (docs axis) select `ancestor.reviewer_comments_per_dim_name` / `_docs` from the graph and carry them into every `chain_history` entry, which `graph_ops.py:18251` / `:25118` attach to the refine item and pass into the trigger; the field therefore has a reader §5 does not account for.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every §5 anchor resolves against the tree: `imas_codex/standard_names/review/checks.py` exists and is the taxonomy loader, `review_checks.yaml` resolves at `imas_codex/llm/prompts/sn/review_checks.yaml`, the retired fields are real (`refine_trigger_keywords` at `fanout/config.py:95`, `refine_trigger_comment_dims` at `:115`, `refine_trigger_comment_chars` at `:126`), and their only reader is `workers.py:7304` (`should_trigger_fanout`, defined at `fanout/trigger.py:105`).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §5's done-when requires a refine rotation "driven by comments", while the same section asserts the comment field has no reader and retires the comment-driven path, so the control arm the done-when names cannot exist once the node's own change lands.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §5 names no gate log of its own, matching the plan's house convention where the prototype's evidence fragment lives in the landed-evidence archive; nothing in §5 points at a scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §5 introduces no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags into symbols or comments; the new `conforming` field is named by what it holds.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §5's claim that "no code path reads" the free-text comment field is contradicted by the code it does not cite: `chain_history.py` selects `ancestor.reviewer_comments_per_dim_name` (and `_docs`) into each ancestor refine-context entry.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 carries one deliverable (make refine and the fanout trigger read the failed checks instead of reviewer prose); §7 no longer re-claims the comment-keyword trigger deletion, so the deletion is owned once.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §5 declares `depends-on` §3 and §4 (both exist and are the askers of the per-check probabilities the trigger reduces over), and §7 explicitly yields the comment-keyword trigger to §5, so no dependency is missing and none points at the wrong node.
